THE DEFECT: across the WHOLE shipped corpus, not one symbol signature referenced any struct its own descriptor declared. `sys/stat.json` declared `struct stat` with FOUR per-target variants and then spelled `fstat`/`lstat`/`stat` (and the eight pe `_stat*` rows) over `ptr<void>`; `time.json` declared `struct tm` and `struct timespec` per format and spelled `localtime`/`gmtime`/`mktime`/`strftime`/`localtime_r`/`nanosleep` over `ptr<void>`. So the descriptor mechanism that exists to TYPE a shipped library's surface asserted nothing about either of them. ★★ WHY THE SIBLING EXAMPLES COULD NOT CATCH IT: `shipped_sys_stat`, `shipped_struct_stat_x86/arm64` and `shipped_stat_macho` all declare a `struct stat`, pass it to `fstat` and read a field back, and every one of them passed throughout the defect — C converts `struct stat *` to `void *` silently, so a call written the ordinary way compiles identically against either spelling. ★★ THE TWO HALVES ARE NOT EQUALLY OBSERVABLE AND THIS ENTRY SAYS SO RATHER THAN PRETENDING: a RETURN type shows up in an expression's type, so `sizeof(*localtime(&t))` interrogates it — unevaluated, so no clock is read and no static buffer is touched, answering `sizeof(void)` (1, or a hard refusal) versus the platform's own record. A PARAMETER type has NO runtime signature at all, so the `stat`/`fstat`/`lstat` half is pinned as a REFUSAL at the semantic tier by `ShippedStatTypedSurface.*` in `tests/ffi/test_shipped_stat_typed_surface.cpp`, beside its accepting twin. ★ THE SECOND ARM IS A FIELD OFFSET, NOT A SIZE, for the reason `shipped_stat_macho` records: macho and x86-64-elf are BOTH 144 bytes, so sizeof cannot discriminate. `st_mode` diverges in offset AND width on every leg — ✔MEASURED BY EXECUTION on three: u32@24 on x86-64 glibc (gcc 13.3.0 native), u32@16 on aarch64 glibc (cross gcc under qemu-aarch64), u16@6 on pe/UCRT (mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 native), and u16@4 on Darwin (Apple clang 21.0.0, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, measured on the operator's own hardware) — all FOUR legs measured, not three. `.` is a directory on all four legs, and the NEGATIVE (`S_ISREG` false) is asserted too so a mode that degenerated to 0 reds instead of passing by accident. ★ AGNOSTIC BY CONSTRUCTION — NOT ONE size or offset literal appears in the source: `struct tm` is 56 bytes on glibc and on Darwin and 36 on the UCRT (all ✔MEASURED) and `struct stat` is 144 / 128 / 48 / 144 (all four ✔MEASURED BY EXECUTION, the macho 144 having a COMPLETELY different field order from the x86-64-elf 144), and both sides of every comparison derive from the same declared type. ★ THE pe LEG ALSO EXERCISES THE UCRT NAME SPLIT the retype had to get right: `stat` imports `_stat64i32` and takes `struct stat *`, while the underscore rows `_stat64i32`/`_fstat64i32`/`_wstat64i32` take `struct _stat *` and `_stat64`/`_fstat64`/`_wstat64` take `struct _stat64 *` — three DISTINCT tags of two distinct layouts, exactly as the UCRT's own <sys/stat.h> has it (its inline `stat()` forwarder CASTS `struct stat *` to `struct _stat64i32 *`, which is the reference's own admission that they are not the same type). RED-ON-DISABLE (REMOVE direction, over the shipped descriptor; NO rebuild needed — the config snapshot is taken at ctest RUN time): restore `time.json`'s `localtime` rows to "fn(ptr<void>) -> ptr<void>" and this example reds on every leg while `shipped_time`, `shipped_time_64bit` and `shipped_sys_stat` stay GREEN, which is the attribution split that makes this entry worth its own directory. ⓘ STATED PLAINLY: restoring `sys/stat.json`'s `stat` row to `ptr<void>` leaves this file GREEN — a parameter type has nothing runnable to observe — and that arm is red-on-disabled in the fixture instead.
